hero.lead: A nation of 41.8 million at the southern tip of Arabia, where seven in ten people are food insecure and the World Bank launched a new partnership with $285 million in June 2026.

capital.heading: Grants that keep a nation fed, and a partnership to build again.

register.name: EU humanitarian funding for Yemen, 2026
register.detail: Additional €22.5 million released 23 October 2026 · planned EU humanitarian support for 2026 now €110 million
register.note: Food security and nutrition, health, water, sanitation and hygiene, protection
register.text: The European Commission’s planned humanitarian support for Yemen in 2026, raised by €22.5 million on 23 October 2026. It finances food security and nutrition, health, water, sanitation and hygiene, protection and other life-saving support, and so serves the food, water and health standards.

register.name: WFP emergency food assistance in Yemen
register.detail: Required to cover operations up to March 2027 · 1.7 million people supported · up to 1.5 million more as access allows
register.note: 18.3 million people face acute food insecurity
register.text: What the World Food Programme states it urgently requires to keep its operations in Yemen running to March 2027. WFP supports 1.7 million vulnerable people in Government-controlled areas and stands ready to reach up to 1.5 million more as access allows. It serves the food standard directly.

register.name: Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026
register.detail: Launched 18 March 2026 · 12 million people targeted, 9.4 million prioritised in the highest-severity areas
register.note: 22.3 million people require humanitarian assistance and protection
register.text: The appeal of the United Nations and humanitarian partners for life-saving assistance and protection across Yemen in 2026. Partners aim to reach 12 million people, putting 9.4 million in the highest-severity areas first. Its life-saving assistance reaches the food, water, health and shelter standards.

register.name: UNICEF Humanitarian Action for Children, Yemen 2026
register.detail: Published 18 March 2026 · 5.2 million people to be reached, including 3.5 million children
register.note: About 19.7 million people, including 15 million women and children, require assistance
register.text: UNICEF’s 2026 appeal for Yemen, to bring essential services to 5.2 million people, among them 3.5 million children. It serves the health, water, food and education standards for children and their mothers.

register.name: Climate Water Information Management and Early Warning Systems (CWIMEWS)
register.detail: Approved by the GCF Board 27 October 2026 (B.46) · GCF grant USD 24.73 million · total USD 28.4 million with co-financing · World Bank the accredited entity
register.note: Nine priority basins; warnings by SMS, radio, sirens and mosque loudspeakers
register.text: A Green Climate Fund grant, through the World Bank, to restore climate and water monitoring in nine priority basins and build a national multi-hazard early warning system for floods, drought, extreme heat and groundwater depletion. It protects the water and food standards and is handed to the Ministry of Water and Environment in phases.

register.name: Cash for Nutrition and Livelihoods Project
register.detail: IDA grant approved 30 June 2026 · implemented by UNICEF with the Social Fund for Development · 15 governorates
register.note: 1.8 million people, at least half of them women
register.text: An IDA grant for vulnerable households in the first 1,000 days of life, focused on new mothers and children under two, with Village Savings and Loan Associations for about 55,000 people and national ID cards and birth certificates for more than 675,000. It serves the food, health and livelihood standards.

register.name: Country Partnership Framework and projects
register.text: Projects for better livelihoods and more jobs amid fragility.

register.name: Financial inclusion and education
register.detail: Approved 17 June 2025 · $20 million Yemen Financial Market Infrastructure and Inclusion Project (UNDP) · $10 million Sustaining Education and Learning Project (UNICEF)
register.text: Two World Bank grants approved in June 2025. The first builds digital payment systems, including a Fast Payment System and a Real Time Gross Settlement System under the Central Bank in Aden, to digitise cash transfers, government payments and remittances; the second keeps schools open in vulnerable districts, with a focus on girls in rural areas. They serve the livelihood and education standards.
register.note: Digital payments under the Central Bank in Aden; schools kept open in vulnerable districts

register.name: Technical Education and Vocational Training Institute, Turbah
register.detail: Grant agreement signed 23 June 2026 · Islamic Development Bank and Kuwait Fund for Arab Economic Development
register.note: Technical and vocational education for young women and men
register.text: A grant to strengthen the capacity of the technical and vocational institute in Turbah, so that more young Yemenis gain quality technical and vocational education. It serves the education and livelihood standards.
by: Kuwait Fund for Arab Economic Development

register.name: Primary health care and cholera response
register.detail: Reported 25 March 2026 · Government of Japan grant through UNICEF
register.note: More than 150,000 people reached with essential health and nutrition services
register.text: A grant from the Government of Japan, delivered by UNICEF, for essential medicines, vaccines, operating support and incentives for health workers in primary health care facilities, with training in cholera case management. It serves the health standard.

register.name: Salary support to the Government of Yemen
register.detail: Reported 26 February 2026 · SR1.3 billion paid by the Saudi Development and Reconstruction Program for Yemen
register.note: Budget support for government salaries; serves no single standard
register.text: A payment by the Saudi Development and Reconstruction Program for Yemen to help meet a shortfall in the salaries of Yemeni government employees. It is budget support and serves no single standard on its own.
by: Saudi Development and Reconstruction Program for Yemen

register.name: Development projects package, 28 projects
register.detail: Announced 14 January 2026 · SR1.9 billion (about US$506 million) · health, energy, education and transport in ten governorates
register.note: 30 schools, a hospital on Socotra, a desalination plant, fuel grants for power plants
register.text: A package of 28 development projects to be financed by the Saudi Development and Reconstruction Program for Yemen, including building and equipping 30 schools, opening a hospital on Socotra, a desalination plant and a new grant of petroleum products to run power plants. It serves the education, health, water and energy standards.
by: Saudi Development and Reconstruction Program for Yemen

register.name: UST teaching hospital, Aden
register.detail: IFC board approval 18 July 2024 · signed 21 December 2024 · US$22 million A loan for IFC’s own account · project cost about US$55 to 60 million
register.note: A 250-bed teaching hospital beside the UST medical college
register.text: An IFC loan to Al-Mawarid International Company for Educational and Health Services to build a 250-bed teaching hospital beside the University of Science and Technology campus in Aden, with a 68-bed inpatient department in the first phase. It serves the health and education standards.
by: Al-Mawarid International Company for Educational and Health Services

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 41% are under fifteen: one of the youngest nations on earth.

items.name: The Diaspora
items.label: Of GDP sent home by citizens abroad, 2016
items.text: Yemenis working abroad send home an eighth of the economy: the lifeline of millions of families.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Terraced highlands of coffee, grain and qat, farmed for three thousand years.

items.name: The Visitors
items.label: Of export earnings from visitors, 2016
items.text: Sana’a’s old city, Shibam and Socotra: wonders the world will one day return to see.

items.name: The Land
items.label: Land area, 2023
items.text: Territory to farm, power and protect.

items.name: Solar Care
items.text: A small Yemeni business that cleans and maintains solar panels for homes and small businesses with dry-cleaning tools instead of water; its team can clean up to six hundred panels in four hours.

items.name: Dorri
items.text: Makes sensory learning toys from fabric and wood to support early childhood development; its products are used in dozens of kindergartens.

items.name: Al-Amal Microfinance Bank
items.text: A microfinance bank serving more than 330,000 clients, 35% of them women, with loans, entrepreneurship coaching and green finance for solar energy, climate-smart agriculture and water conservation.

items.name: ONE Cash
items.text: A digital wallet for individuals and businesses in Yemen to pay, receive and transfer money, with more than 850,000 active customers and about 80,000 merchants; its transactions grew 32% in 2025 to around $3.3 billion.

items.name: Jawali (WeCash)
items.text: A mobile wallet through which Yemenis receive salaries and aid payments, transfer money, make purchases and pay bills without a conventional bank account.

items.name: Qima Coffee
items.text: A specialty coffee exporter that buys directly from Yemeni smallholders, paying its farmer partners on average more than 400% above the standard international market price; its processing centre has benefited more than 1,500 producers.
